Filed as #49281, @barthap.

It carries the failing-`BEGIN` test and the repro you asked for, plus measurements on the two things you flagged. Short version: `SQLITE_BUSY` today is worse than it looks, because the stray `ROLLBACK` replaces the error that would tell a caller to retry (`cannot rollback - no transaction is active` instead of `database is locked`), so moving `BEGIN` out of the `try` is what makes a busy database reportable at all, before any retry policy exists.

One thing worth flagging up front: guarding the `ROLLBACK` on `isInTransaction*` looks like the obvious fix and it does not work. That is `sqlite3_get_autocommit`, a property of the connection rather than of the call, so when our `BEGIN` fails because someone else's transaction is open, the guard reads "in a transaction" and lets the destructive `ROLLBACK` through anyway. I measured all three shapes side by side in the issue.

I left `SAVEPOINT` and the error-preservation question open rather than picking for you. Happy to turn it into a PR once you have settled the design, or to leave it entirely with your team.
